L22: 【8†Lemma 43.23.1.】 Let $V$ be a vector space of dimension $n + 1$. Let $X \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ be a closed subscheme. If $X \not= \mathbf{P}(V)$, then there is a nonempty Zariski open $U \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ such that for all closed points $p \in U$ the restriction of the projection $r_ p$ defines a finite morphism $r_ p|_ X : X \to \mathbf{P}(W_ p)$.
L23: Proof. We claim the lemma holds with $U = \mathbf{P}(V) \setminus X$. For a closed point $p$ of $U$ we indeed obtain a morphism $r_ p|_ X : X \to \mathbf{P}(W_ p)$. This morphism is proper because $X$ is a proper scheme (Morphisms, Lemmas 【14†29.44.5】 and 【15†29.42.7】). On the other hand, the fibres of $r_ p$ are affine lines as can be seen by a direct calculation. Hence the fibres of $r_ p|X$ are proper and affine, whence finite (Morphisms, Lemma 【16†29.45.11】).
L24: Finally, a proper morphism with finite fibres is finite (Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 【17†30.21.1】). $\square$

L23: 【8†Lemma 43.23.2.】 Let $V$ be a vector space of dimension $n + 1$. Let $X \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ be a closed subvariety. Let $x \in X$ be a nonsingular point.
L24: 
L25:   1. If $\dim (X) < n - 1$, then there is a nonempty Zariski open $U \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ such that for all closed points $p \in U$ the morphism $r_ p|_ X : X \to r_ p(X)$ is an isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of $r_ p(x)$.
L26:   2. If $\dim (X) = n - 1$, then there is a nonempty Zariski open $U \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ such that for all closed points $p \in U$ the morphism $r_ p|_ X : X \to \mathbf{P}(W_ p)$ is étale at $x$.
L27: 
L28: Proof. Proof of (1). Note that if $x, y \in X$ have the same image under $r_ p$ then $p$ is on the line $\overline{xy}$. Consider the finite type scheme
L29: 
L30: \[ T = \{ (y, p) \mid y \in X \setminus \{ x\} ,\ p \in \mathbf{P}(V),\ p \in \overline{xy}\} \]
L31: and the morphisms $T \to X$ and $T \to \mathbf{P}(V)$ given by $(y, p) \mapsto y$ and $(y, p) \mapsto p$. Since each fibre of $T \to X$ is a line, we see that the dimension of $T$ is $\dim (X) + 1 < \dim (\mathbf{P}(V))$. Hence $T \to \mathbf{P}(V)$ is not surjective. On the other hand, consider the finite type scheme
L32: 
L33: \[ T' = \{ p \mid p \in \mathbf{P}(V) \setminus \{ x\} , \ \overline{xp}\text{ tangent to }X\text{ at }x\} \]
L34: Then the dimension of $T'$ is $\dim (X) < \dim (\mathbf{P}(V))$. Thus the morphism $T' \to \mathbf{P}(V)$ is not surjective either. Let $U \subset \mathbf{P}(V) \setminus X$ be nonempty open and disjoint from these images; such a $U$ exists because the images of $T$ and $T'$ in $\mathbf{P}(V)$ are constructible by Morphisms, Lemma 【15†29.23.2】. Then for $p \in U$ closed the projection $r_ p|_ X : X \to \mathbf{P}(W_ p)$ is injective on the tangent space at $x$ and $r_ p^{-1}(\{ r_ p(x)\} ) = \{ x\} $.
L35: This means that $r_ p$ is unramified at $x$ (Varieties, Lemma 【16†33.16.8】), finite by Lemma 【10†43.23.1】, and $r_ p^{-1}(\{ r_ p(x)\} ) = \{ x\} $ thus Étale Morphisms, Lemma 【17†41.7.3】 applies and there is an open neighbourhood $R$ of $r_ p(x)$ in $\mathbf{P}(W_ p)$ such that $(r_ p|_ X)^{-1}(R) \to R$ is a closed immersion which proves (1).
L36: Proof of (2). In this case we still conclude that the morphism $T' \to \mathbf{P}(V)$ is not surjective. Arguing as above we conclude that for $U \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ avoiding $X$ and the image of $T'$, the projection $r_ p|_ X : X \to \mathbf{P}(W_ p)$ is étale at $x$ and finite. $\square$

L23: 【8†Lemma 37.44.1.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent:
L24:   1. $f$ is finite,
L25: 
L26:   2. $f$ is proper with finite fibres,
L27: 
L28:   3. $f$ is proper and locally quasi-finite,
L29: 
L30:   4. $f$ is universally closed, separated, locally of finite type and has finite fibres.
L31: 
L32: Proof. We have (1) implies (2) by Morphisms, Lemmas 【14†29.45.11】, 【15†29.21.10】, and 【16†29.45.10】. We have (2) implies (3) by Morphisms, Lemma 【17†29.21.7】. We have (3) implies (4) by the definition of proper morphisms and Morphisms, Lemmas 【18†29.21.9】 and 【15†29.21.10】.
L33: Assume (4). Pick $s \in S$. By Morphisms, Lemma 【17†29.21.7】 we see that all the finitely many points of $X_ s$ are isolated in $X_ s$. Choose an elementary étale neighbourhood $(U, u) \to (S, s)$ and decomposition $X_ U = V \amalg W$ as in Lemma 【19†37.41.6】. Note that $W_ u = \emptyset $ because all points of $X_ s$ are isolated. Since $f$ is universally closed we see that the image of $W$ in $U$ is a closed set not containing $u$. After shrinking $U$ we may assume that $W = \emptyset $.
L34: In other words we see that $X_ U = V$ is finite over $U$. Since $s \in S$ was arbitrary this means there exists a family $\{ U_ i \to S\} $ of étale morphisms whose images cover $S$ such that the base changes $X_{U_ i} \to U_ i$ are finite. Note that $\{ U_ i \to S\} $ is an étale covering, see Topologies, Definition 【20†34.4.1】. Hence it is an fpqc covering, see Topologies, Lemma 【21†34.9.7】. Hence we conclude $f$ is finite by Descent, Lemma 【22†35.23.25】. $\square$

L22: 【8†Lemma 10.113.1.】 Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime of $S$ lying over the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$. Assume that
L23: 
L24:   1. $R$ is Noetherian,
L25: 
L26:   2. $R \to S$ is of finite type,
L27: 
L28:   3. $R$, $S$ are domains, and
L29: 
L30:   4. $R \subset S$.
L31: 
L32: Then we have
L33: 
L34: \[ \text{height}(\mathfrak q) \leq \text{height}(\mathfrak p) + \text{trdeg}_ R(S) - \text{trdeg}_{\kappa (\mathfrak p)} \kappa (\mathfrak q) \]
L35: 
L36: with equality if $R$ is universally catenary.
L37: Proof. Suppose that $R \subset S' \subset S$, where $S'$ is a finitely generated $R$-subalgebra of $S$. In this case set $\mathfrak q' = S' \cap \mathfrak q$. The lemma for the ring maps $R \to S'$ and $S' \to S$ implies the lemma for $R \to S$ by additivity of transcendence degree in towers of fields (Fields, Lemma 【14†9.26.5】). Hence we can use induction on the number of generators of $S$ over $R$ and reduce to the case where $S$ is generated by one element over $R$.
L38: Case I: $S = R[x]$ is a polynomial algebra over $R$. In this case we have $\text{trdeg}_ R(S) = 1$. Also $R \to S$ is flat and hence
L39: 
L40: \[ \dim (S_{\mathfrak q}) = \dim (R_{\mathfrak p}) + \dim (S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}) \]
L41: see Lemma 【15†10.112.7】. Let $\mathfrak r = \mathfrak pS$. Then $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa (\mathfrak p)} \kappa (\mathfrak q) = 1$ is equivalent to $\mathfrak q = \mathfrak r$, and implies that $\dim (S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}) = 0$. In the same vein $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa (\mathfrak p)} \kappa (\mathfrak q) = 0$ is equivalent to having a strict inclusion $\mathfrak r \subset \mathfrak q$, which implies that $\dim (S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}) = 1$.
L42: Thus we are done with case I with equality in every instance.
L43: Case II: $S = R[x]/\mathfrak n$ with $\mathfrak n \not= 0$. In this case we have $\text{trdeg}_ R(S) = 0$. Denote $\mathfrak q' \subset R[x]$ the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$. Thus we have
L44: 
L45: \[ S_{\mathfrak q} = (R[x])_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak n(R[x])_{\mathfrak q'} \]
L46: By the previous case we have $\dim ((R[x])_{\mathfrak q'}) = \dim (R_{\mathfrak p}) + 1 - \text{trdeg}_{\kappa (\mathfrak p)} \kappa (\mathfrak q)$. Since $\mathfrak n \not= 0$ we see that the dimension of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ decreases by at least one, see Lemma 【16†10.60.13】, which proves the inequality of the lemma.
L47: To see the equality in case $R$ is universally catenary note that $\mathfrak n \subset R[x]$ is a height one prime as it corresponds to a nonzero prime in $F[x]$ where $F$ is the fraction field of $R$. Hence any maximal chain of primes in $S_\mathfrak q = R[x]_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak nR[x]_{\mathfrak q'}$ corresponds to a maximal chain of primes with length 1 greater between $\mathfrak q'$ and $(0)$ in $R[x]$.
L48: If $R$ is universally catenary these all have the same length equal to the height of $\mathfrak q'$. This proves that $\dim (S_\mathfrak q) = \dim (R[x]_{\mathfrak q'}) - 1$ and this implies equality holds as desired. $\square$
